Apple powdery mildew

By Gafar Laiya, Gujarat Bio Organics · Updated 2026-11-25

Apple powdery mildew coats young shoot tips, leaves and flowers with white floury fungus, stunting shoots and russeting fruit. Cut out white shoot tips during winter pruning, and spray wettable sulphur or myclobutanil as per label, keeping sulphur 14–21 days apart from horticultural mineral oil (Dr. YSP UHF).

Symptoms

  • White, powdery growth on young leaves and shoot tips; leaves narrow and curl.
  • Infected buds open late and weak; fruit can show net-like russet.

Control

  1. In winter pruning, cut off shoot tips that look white or silvery; the fungus overwinters there.
  2. From pink bud through early summer, spray wettable sulphur or myclobutanil at label doses.
  3. Never spray sulphur within 14–21 days of horticultural mineral oil: the combination burns leaves.
  4. No sprays at full bloom.

Pesticide safety: Use only pesticides registered for apple by CIB&RC, at the dose and waiting period on the label, and follow your state's current spray schedule (SKUAST-K, Dr. YSP UHF or the state horticulture department).

Questions farmers ask

What causes white powder on apple leaves?

Apple powdery mildew, a fungus that overwinters in shoot tips.

How do I control powdery mildew in apple?

Remove white tips in winter pruning and spray wettable sulphur or myclobutanil as per label, keeping sulphur 14–21 days away from oil sprays.
